**Published native reproduction:** official `pm-gantt-chart@2026.11.18` with `@unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.14` and `2026.11.19`, Node 24.22.3, in disposable no-Git trackers. Activate pm-gantt-chart in an initialized tracker, then run:

```sh
printf '{broken' > broken.json
pm gantt drift --before broken.json --after broken.json --json
```

Both hosts exit 2 with `extension_read_output_invalid` rather than the invalid-snapshot diagnostic. The .19 response tells the caller to return a `moved` collection, although the requested repair is to supply valid snapshot JSON. As a control, a valid version-1 snapshot compared against itself succeeds on both hosts (`ok: true`, `moved: []`). This is a misleading refusal, not evidence of a successful comparison or data loss, and it predates the dependency bump in [#251](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/pull/251). Its [CI](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/actions/runs/44573342418/job/135734079527) also exposes the missing-row refusal in the direct SDK harness.

The [shipped handler](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/v2026.11.18/index.ts#L3219-L3235) declares `moved` on the read output but returns a different shape for invalid inputs. The [typed input loader](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-gantt-chart/blob/v2026.11.18/schedule-files.ts) provides `invalid_estimate` and a remedy; current output validation replaces it.

**Acceptance:** Keep exit 2 and the specific input code/remedy for malformed, missing and oversized snapshot inputs in the native CLI and SDK. Keep `moved` validation and normal row/budget behavior for successful comparisons. Independently probe the packed artifact and verify that refusal and valid-empty comparison leave tracker data unchanged.
gantt drift masks invalid snapshot input with a missing moved-row error
